title: Compact button outline and accent resilience for high-density dark tables and charts
creator: Aisha Moreno
description:
Problem statement: Compact density surfaces (tables, small card lists, and inline controls) in our deep/dim dark themes currently lose button affordance and chart stroke contrast when teams apply brand accents. On small controls the existing focus/outline tokens become visually noisy or invisible depending on brand tint. This ticket proposes an outline/accent-resilience system: a layered outline token set and a contrast-aware accent modulation function that dynamically chooses outline weight and neutral anchor when brand tint conflicts with low-contrast surfaces. Goals are to preserve affordance, maintain >=3:1 interaction contrast for compact buttons, and avoid adding visible noise on dense data grids and sparklines.

Scope: design tokens for outline/interaction ink at 10,12,14px control sizes; component overrides for Button (compact/ghost/primary), Table rows (zebra/hover/focus), and Line/Bar chart strokes used at small thicknesses. Deliverables: token spec (values + usage rules), component CSS/token mapping table, 2 Figma mock pages (compact table and micro-controls), interaction guidelines for product teams, and QA checklist for accessibility and visual regression tests.
acceptance_criteria:
- Token spec published to tokens repo and linked in console theming docs
- Compact Button variants show >=3:1 contrast for normal/focus/hover states across 6 representative brand tints
- Table zebra and focused row maintain row hierarchy without outline bleeding into adjacent rows at 8px row gap
- Chart micro-strokes remain distinct from gridlines at typical render widths (0.8–1.5px) for dark themes
- Design approvals from PM and Accessibility (a11y) sign-off present
- Implementation PR with visual snapshots merged
tasks: Audit current outline and focus tokens across Console dark themes
Create layered-outline token proposal (neutral anchor + tint-safe rim + interaction ink) in tokens spec
Design Figma mocks: compact controls, dense table, micro-chart variants
Prototype CSS overrides in storybook for Button and Table small density
Run contrast matrix for 6 brand tints and document failures
Iterate with frontend on performance trade-offs for box-shadow vs border outlines
Prepare QA checklist and visual regression snapshots
comments: 2025-02-20 - Aisha Moreno: Initial ticket created after design crit. Noted multiple reports from Platform and Observability teams about ‘lost’ compact actions in deep dark theme when customers enable brand accents.

2025-02-24 - Lukas Chen: Did a quick audit; ghost buttons use 1px translucent white outline which disappears against some purple/teal brand tints. Attaching sample screenshots and a minimal CSS reproduction in storybook branch.

2025-02-27 - Accessibility (Priya Rao): Recommend layered approach — a subtle neutral anchor under a tint-adaptive rim to preserve color semantics without adding noise for dense UIs. Need to validate against 3:1 minimum for small controls.

2025-02-28 - PM (Marco Silva): Customer impact rated medium for dashboard users; schedule in Cycle 2025-W09. Prioritize the Button and Table changes in first pass; charts to follow if token shape is settled.

2025-03-02 - Design review: Decided to use three outline token roles: outline.anchor (neutral, shadow-like), outline.rim (tint-aware but clamped contrast), outline.focus (interaction ink). Also agreed on clipping rules for table rows to avoid outline overflow.

2025-03-04 - Lukas Chen: Storybook prototype updated (branch: feat/DES-91234-outline-resilience). PR opened: github.com/redwood-inference/ui/pull/2483. Initial snapshots show improvements but one brand tint (emerald-600) still fails hover contrast for 10px buttons; adjusting rim clamp algorithm.
